decision_rules.recurrence: Complete records and qualified uncertainty exist. Streams 0/1 select the smallest-mean-W consecutive triple centered at 3000..19000 (earliest tie); streams 2/3 re-measure early, basin and late W, and each confirmation stream independently must show early W exceeds basin W by >=2x and >=0.01 Ha, with at least two of 40000/45000/50000 exceeding it by both margins with simultaneous confidence bounds. At least 2 of 3 lineages pass. If two lineages pass and the third is incomplete, the study-level label is unresolved; report recurrence in the two complete lineages only. Tail exceedance safeguards must not contradict the W result: a contradiction is (i) W meets the rise rule while no fixed exceedance threshold shows an increase of at least its own margin in decision_rules.parameters.exceedance_margins_hartree, or (ii) W fails the rise rule, or the bounded-null band excludes it, while some fixed exceedance threshold shows an increase of at least its own margin. A bulk-threshold (0.01/0.05/0.1 Ha) decrease that accompanies a W rise is expected, as He-v1's own 25k-to-50k contrast shows, and is not a contradiction. Directional wording and evidence: operator-review-contract-proposals-20261107 items 1-2 on fffc313a, decided in primary-measure-and-margins-decision-20261107 on 8a67671f from analysis primary-measure-and-margins-analysis-20261107 (FASRC Cannon job 58568904).
decision_rules.bounded_null: All 3 lineages are complete and pass instrument/sampling gates; simultaneous inference over every predeclared basin, checkpoint, threshold, and window search excludes the W decrease/rise rule. For every reference checkpoint k in bounded_null_reference_updates, the simultaneous band excludes W at bounded_null_late_count or more late checkpoints reaching max(2 W(k), W(k) + 0.01 Ha). Fixed-threshold exceedance bands use all four streams and the pilot gate; they also exclude an absolute late increase at every threshold of at least that threshold's own margin in decision_rules.parameters.exceedance_margins_hartree (0.002 Ha at the tail thresholds 0.5 and 1 Ha; 0.01 Ha at the bulk thresholds 0.01, 0.05 and 0.1 Ha, where the pilot gate's half-width <= half-margin requirement is otherwise unreachable). A flat MAD or nonsignificance alone is not equivalence.
decision_rules.unresolved: Any required record, identity, instrument, dependence/uncertainty qualification, tail safeguard, operator decision, or horizon is absent or inconclusive; a partial lineage result, conflicting streams, unsupported margins, or a tail-only change outside the declared instrument is unresolved.

lane_proposals.decided_by: operator-review-contract-proposals-20261107 item 1 on fffc313a ('how much does it matter? decide based on He-v1 analysis', delegated to the lane), lane decision primary-measure-and-margins-decision-20261107 on 8a67671f
lane_proposals.proposal: Use the historical He training basin only as context: 5k-block median of within-batch variance on a changing model, about 0.00173 Ha^2; s10=26570 and s90=44982 are definition-dependent onset summaries whose definition is only in the unopened Netscratch report, not basin-departure points. Use W, the 99.9th percentile of the absolute deviation from the median, as the primary statistic for H, with fixed exceedance probabilities as safeguards (see decision_rules for the directional-contradiction rule and decision_rules.parameters.exceedance_margins_hartree for the per-threshold margins).
lane_proposals.rationale: W detects rare-event frequency defects that MAD can hide; no fresh He basin checkpoint exists for a common-estimand threshold. Evidence (primary-measure-and-margins-analysis-20261107, Cannon job 58568904): He-v1's own 25k-to-50k fresh-evaluation contrast is a 22-25x W rise, detected identically by W and by the tail exceedance thresholds (0.5, 1 Ha), while the bulk exceedance thresholds (0.01, 0.05, 0.1 Ha) FALL at the same transition -- an exceedance-primary rule on the bulk thresholds would have called He-v1's broken checkpoint an improvement. For an He-v1-sized effect the choice of primary statistic does not change the outcome; for moderate tail-onset versus uniform-broadening effects it does, which is why the primary stays a ratio statistic (W) rather than a threshold in hartree.
alternatives: make exceedance probability the primary axis instead of percentile W
use a separately approved recomputed He fresh-evaluation reference

lane_proposals.decided_by: operator-review-contract-proposals-20261107 items 3 and 5 on fffc313a, quoted 'whatever He-v1 did we do in Hydrogen experiment' (item 3, correcting an earlier 'trainable' answer) and 'whatever He-v1 did' (item 5)
lane_proposals.proposal: Match He-v1 exactly, adapted only where the one-electron system forces a deviation. Primary source: experiments/atomistic/he-v1/configs/train.yaml at the executed He-v1 training source commit 418accf153368aab45586dc2a2cc97c18472691c (REPORT.md line 5 names this as the commit of record for train-seed0000/Cannon job 40907434). As resolved there: one TPENLayer, Embedding max_order=2/out_channels=32/hidden_channels=128/num_hidden_layers=1 (lines 110-116), EquivariantMixing and PathAggregation both max_order=2/max_virtual_order=2/channels=32/SiLU (lines 118-135), ResidualUpdater (line 137); post-readout factors are ElectronElectronCusp(trainable_range=true) plus ElectronNucleusCusp with CurvatureElectronNucleusCuspLaw(curvature_coefficient=0.01, curvature_range=1.0, trainable=true) (lines 188-197); PfaffianReadout(channels=32, trainable=true) (lines 198-227); optimizer torch.optim.Adam(lr=0.005) (lines 277-280); training sampler MetropolisSampler(n_walkers=4096, burn_in=100, n_steps=10, proposal_scale=0.5) (lines 249-260): burn-in 100, 10 Metropolis steps per update, proposal scale 0.5 bohr. The resolved config of run train-seed0000 itself was not separately available to this amendment; the source commit's train.yaml is the primary evidence used. Nuclear curvature law: c (curvature_coefficient) = 0.01, d (curvature_range) = 1.0, both trainable -- this already matches the contract's normalizability_gate notation (outer slope -1 + c/d, exact_hydrogen_answer c=0) and required no numeric change. One-electron-forced deviations from He-v1, recorded because H has one electron where He has two: (1) ElectronElectronCusp has no effect for a single electron (no electron pair exists to carry same-spin or opposite-spin range gradient; the factor's channel is structurally inert, not frozen by training as He's same-spin channel is for a singlet) -- it is retained as a declared factor for parsed-config agreement with He-v1's pattern, not because it changes the H-v2 wavefunction; (2) spin configuration is n_up=1, n_down=0 (He-v1: n_up=1, n_down=1); (3) nuclear_charge is 1 (He-v1: 2), per study.nuclear_charge; (4) the PfaffianReadout's odd-electron border is retained as a readout device rather than a second electron, as already documented in README.md.
lane_proposals.rationale: A concrete model/optimizer/sampler proposal makes the pipeline and science plan reviewable without silently choosing unreviewed hyperparameters; c=0 is the exact hydrogen answer and c/d drift is a reportable normalizability signal. Matching He-v1 exactly (rather than re-deriving hyperparameters) is now an operator decision, not a lane proposal, so comparability between the He-v1 and H-v2 wavefunction families is by construction wherever the one-electron system does not force a difference.
alternatives: a revised architecture or optimizer with changed recurrence and resource implications stated
